title: WPMS/2067/2022 of RUBY CHAUDHARY Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2067 of 2022
Ruby Chaudhary ..................Petitioner

-Versus-State of Uttarakhand and Others ....................Respondents
Present: Mr. Gaurav Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Pradeep Hairiya, learned Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Date of Hearing and Order: 05.09.2022
Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court has
passed the following order:-
1. By filing this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for
the following reliefs:-
i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus commanding the respondent no. 2 and 3
to issue a caste certificate of Other Backward Class
(in short OBC) in favour of the petitioner after taking
into consideration the application and other
documents submitted by the petitioner before the
Tehsildar, Haridwar, District Haridwar.

2
ii. Issue any suitable writ, order or direction, which
this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under
the facts and circumstances of the case.
iii. Award the cost of the petition to the petitioner.
2. It is apparent from the record that the petitioner's
application for issuance of caste certificate was rejected
by the Authorities - Tehsildar, Haridwar on the report
dated 17.02.2021 of the Revenue Sub Inspector, Kangdi
on the ground that the petitioner could not produce any
document that she is residing in the State of
Uttarakhand since 1985. The application of the
petitioner has been rejected without a proper application
of mind. When the case of the petitioner is that she was
born in the year 1990 and her father was a resident of
the State of Uttarakhand, it was unreasonable on the
part of the Revenue Authorities to seek proof of her
residence in the State of Uttarakhand from 1985. In
fact, the case of the present petitioner is covered by
Circular dated 02.04.2013 bearing No. 1118/XVII-1/2013-01(20)/2013, wherein at Paragraph No. 4 the
following provisions have been made, which reads as
under:-

3. It is also apparent that the case of the petitioner comes
within Clause b, sub-paragraph (i) and (ii) of Paragraph

5
No. 4 of the above Circular. Thus, the writ petition is
allowed.
4. The Tehsildar, Haridwar - respondent no. 3 is directed
to reconsider the matter, and affording reasonable
opportunity of hearing and production of documents, to
the petitioner to establish that her father was a resident
of the State of Uttarakhand, in terms of the provisions
referred to above and take a decision strictly, in
accordance with law, by speaking and reasoned order
within a period of 21 days from production of certified
copy of this order along with copy of the brief to the writ
petition.
 (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
